examples.solution_text:
$\angle PAB=72^{\circ}$ (alternate segment theorem)

$\angle APY=46^{\circ}$ (alternate segment theorem)

$\angle APB=180^{\circ}-72^{\circ}-46^{\circ}$ (angle sum of a triangle)

$\angle APB=62^{\circ}$

$\angle APB=\angle PBA$ (base angles of an isosceles triangle)

$\angle PBA=\frac{180^{\circ}-76^{\circ}}{2}$ (angle sum of a triangle)

$\angle PBA=52^{\circ}$

$\angle APY=52^{\circ}$ (alternate segment theorem)

$\angle OCB=90^{\circ}-x$ (a tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact)

$OC=OB$ (radii)

$\angle OBC=90^{\circ}-x$ (base angles of an isosceles triangle)

$\angle COB=180^{\circ}-2(90^{\circ}-x)$ (angle sum of a triangle)

$\angle COB=2x$

$\angle CAB=\frac{1}{2}\angle COB$ (angle at the centre is double the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc)

$\angle CAB=x$

$\therefore\angle BCQ=\angle CAB$

$A$ lies in the alternate segment, on the opposite side of chord $PB$ from the marked tangent-chord angle.

$\angle PAB=54^{\circ}$ (alternate segment theorem)
